description: Issue #841: _EtlRunLogController had no OnActionExecuting role gate at all (grep -c OnActionExecuting == 0), only page-level URL-RBAC -- and its Rerun action starts a real pipeline re-execution from a watermark snapshot. This mutant neutralizes the newly-added gate's `if (!isAdmin)` check to `if (false)`, so context.Result = Forbid() is never reached and every caller passes through unconditionally, reproducing the pre-fix behaviour. Checked against EtlControllerGateHttpTests.EtlRunLogController_Index_NonAdmin_Forbidden, which authenticates as a real user with zero FrameworkRole grants and asserts the response is the gate's AccessDenied redirect -- with the mutant applied, the assertion fails because the response is no longer that redirect. The green control is an unrelated test in the same test_project (EtlTenantIsolationTests.EtlDeadLetterRow_TenantA_CanReadOwnRow), proving the mutation's build/test environment itself is not broken -- the positive control for the GATE LOGIC specifically lives as a unit test in a different project, EtlRbacTests.EtlRunLogController_OnActionExecuting_ETLAdmin_role_is_allowed, which run_mutant.py's single test_project field cannot reference from this same entry; see EtlControllerGateHttpTests.cs's class-level doc comment for why a real-HTTP positive control is not currently achievable for any WalkingTec.Mvvm.Etl controller (a separate, pre-existing, already-filed defect).
